label: Carnivore herbivore dentition comparison
adaptation_note: Separate jaw orientation views and all selected crown groups at a common detail scale. Source tooth identities, attachments and pointed-versus-grinding distinctions retained; not a complete formula or measured skull.
acceptance_requirement: Preserve which tooth belongs to which jaw and the intended shape comparison. Do not replace distinct teeth with continuous bands or imply an exact measured specimen.

frames.title: Dog jaw orientation overview
frames.teaching_key: Dog lateral jaw orientation: snout to the right, upper jaw above lower jaw. Orbital detail is omitted in the horse orientation view to avoid a false boundary contact. Teeth are intentionally absent from this orientation view and supplied by the immediately following crown details. Selected fully permanent domestic dog. Visible representative incisors are not the complete dental formula. This is an introduced schematic, not a measured individual specimen.

frames.title: Dog upper crowns 1–3
frames.teaching_key: Dog, upper jaw; back-to-front order left to right: dog-upper-M2, dog-upper-M1, dog-upper-P4. All crown details use 0.45 native pins per source unit before rounding. Teeth attach intentionally to the short jaw-edge reference. Upper crowns point down and lower crowns up. This selected crown inventory is not a complete tooth formula or measured specimen. Compare pointed canines/cutting forms with the broader horse cheek crowns.
